# Independent static review of the new owned Main runner body

Reviewed exact remote-body.py SHA43c699c0d70fa8bf04bf78fd911412eba68600685d84e224d79cf11f370a1d61. This is a static review only: no CONFIG prefix, final five-ELF BOM, upload, Docker execution or target Main/App run occurred. The previous runner body2230 and failed attempt3 remain unchanged.

The actual earlier startup observation race is supported separately by independent observation packetcc8ca3b9b0a33b06d826994aab8da4ab9b0ddf351098cfdfdea927fdb21b9ed4. Its sole authorized no-bind sentinel directly observed initially missing, then created/Pid0, then Running at4.236s. That evidence invalidates the old short fixed polling premise; it is not a business Main acceptance.

The new body has one monotonic30-second startup deadline, caps every startup inspect RPC by the remaining time, and continues through a verified created state. Each inspect saves its selector, full stdout/stderr, return or exception, elapsed time and parsed state. Only explicit Docker NoSuch errors establish temporary absence; permission/daemon/non-NoSuch failures remain errors. The first owner-verified visible container binds the full immutable ID even before Running; later inspections use that ID. Verification checks exact image, task label, UID, netnone, read-only root and the exact bundle/owned mounts before stop/remove.

Cleanup observes an initially absent container for a further bounded10-second window while the Docker client remains alive. Verified containers are stopped, re-inspected, and only that exact owner-verified ID may be removed. Client join/termination, final name and task-label queries, final verified-ID inspection, bundle check and command record are separately guarded. Name/label results are attached before a nonzero status assertion can throw. The final remaining value begins as unknown; False is assigned only after successful name/label and, when bound, full-ID inspection. A never-bound ID after a started client stays unknown even when final queries are empty, so the final success assertion cannot certify that path as reclaimed.

Syntax and recursive symbol-table checks pass;15 structural checks agree with the manual path review. These are source inspection aids, not runtime failure injection or reproduction of the fixed launch. An inspect timeout during startup becomes a failed run with cleanup rather than an unproven Running result. A cleanup/daemon readback failure records failure or unknown and cannot pass the final gate. Late daemon creation beyond the observation window remains a possible failed-run condition requiring exact follow-up readback; this body does not claim it is impossible.

The body may proceed to final CONFIG/five-ELF BOM review when rich integration and current bindings are available. This review alone does not authorize treating its still-unexecuted command/update/timer driver as passed, nor does it validate the final CONFIG, actual live process topology or cleanup under every daemon failure. No true H/P/SDK, ledger or frozen evidence was edited.
